implementation_summary: buildEditedView now rebuilds each kept roadmap item from its kept findings as edited. The title comes from the first kept finding when that finding's title was edited or the item's original first finding was dropped. When any finding of the item was dropped, priority = highest impact, effort = highest effort and phase = ROADMAP_PHASE[priority] (buildRoadmap's rule; ROADMAP_PHASE imported, RANK/highest copied as SCALE_RANK/highestScale because roadmap.ts does not export them). Items with no kept findings still go; items no edit touches stay as recorded with their id and place. 4 regression tests added.

risks: Copied rule: SCALE_RANK/highestScale in edits.ts:449-454 duplicate roadmap.ts RANK/highest (not exported). The roadmap.ts owner should export it (e.g. highestScale) so edits.ts imports it instead of keeping a copy.

Only fields whose inputs changed are recalculated: the title when the first kept finding's title was edited or the first finding was dropped; priority/effort/phase only when a finding was dropped. This gives the same result as always recalculating for pipeline-built roadmaps, and keeps 'no edits = original view' and the shared fixture (whose roadmap is not buildRoadmap output, e.g. RM-2 priority medium but phase 1) unchanged for audit-doc-proposal.test.ts.

No re-sort or renumber after a drop: ids and order stay stable, so a demoted item can sit before a higher-priority one and roadmap.ts's 'phases never go down along the list' may not hold in the edited view. Roadmap document and Proposal group by phase, so they show correctly; the site.json roadmap list order can show this.

Visible behavior change: after a page is removed an item can move to another phase (e.g. 2 to 3) in the Roadmap document, Proposal {{timeline}} and Owner Audit; an edited first-finding title now replaces the item heading everywhere.
Runner audit route suites were not run by me; see tests_proposed.
